page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is a compute-focused instance within Azure's ARM-based family, configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs. Powered by custom Microsoft silicon utilizing the ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture clocked at 3.4 GHz, the instance provides 1 thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic workloads benefit from hardware AES acceleration, though vector extensions such as AVX and AMX are absent on this architecture.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capability. The system scores in the top 25 percent for multi-core evaluations, including stress-ng multi-core throughput (66,293.46), Geekbench multi-core (19,970.0), and Clang software compilation (40,457.0). In contrast, single-threaded execution sits in the median range across Geekbench (1,671.0) and stress-ng (2,073.49). Memory subsystem performance is a primary highlight, with uncached read throughput reaching 449.06 GB/sec and uncached write throughput reaching 188.51 GB/sec, placing memory bandwidth in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems.

The instance does not include local disk storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on remote network storage for persistent file systems. In terms of cost efficiency, the 1:2 memory-to-core ratio maximizes CPU core density, making it resource-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not need high memory capacities. However, larger memory-bound workloads or massive models, such as 70B parameter LLMs, see reduced prompt processing throughput. The D32pls_v6 is best matched for software compilation, static web serving, Redis caching nodes, microservice infrastructure, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated cores running on the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor at 3.4 GHz with 1 thread per core. Configured with 64.0 GB of RAM (a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio) and 128 MB of L3 cache, the system targets compute-dense workloads. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes. Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core compute capability, with top-quartile results in multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench compilation, and compression tasks, supported by top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 449 GB/sec for reads and 188 GB/sec for writes. Single-core performance falls within median tiers. With high core density and balanced resource distribution, the D32pls_v6 is suited for multi-threaded build pipelines, web serving clusters, Redis caching nodes, and parallel microservice workloads that do not demand large per-core memory footprints.
